PlanningFailure: ValueError: PlannerStopped: No supported graph can be formed from the registered tools, for three independent reasons. (1) No registered tool exposes the study JSON's non-data metadata values that the protocol requires: the row-to-role assignment (training / calibration / final assessment), the fitted-model specification and target column, the nominal coverage target, and the finite-sample rank convention. InspectScientificFile returns only the top-level field schema, record count and provenance; QueryScientificRecordsFile preserves non-data metadata in its results_file but never returns those values, and no other tool can read them. (2) No registered tool can turn the study's nested observed_features arrays into a numeric matrix: each record holds a list-valued cell, and ExtractNumericColumns explicitly rejects non-scalar cells. So FitLinearRegression / PredictLinearModel cannot be bound to the archived features. (3) No registered tool performs elementwise vector arithmetic on upstream outputs, and this task needs elementwise work: per-row point predictions, residual = truth - prediction, |residual|, and per-row coverage membership (|residual| <= calibrated radius). ExecuteNumericalCode cannot substitute, because it has no filesystem or network access and its code argument is a literal string that cannot receive upstream arrays or the task file. Needed capability: a split-conformal calibration and coverage evaluator that accepts the study file path and returns the calibration order rank, calibrated radius, common interval width, covered assessment rows and empirical coverage (or, alternatively, a task-file reader that yields typed role metadata plus per-row feature and target arrays, together with an elementwise vector-arithmetic/interval-membership tool).

PlanningFailure: ValueError: PlannerStopped: Missing capability: an input path that delivers the study's complete nested observation table into a computation. The only JSON readers available are InspectScientificFile (schema/counts/provenance only, no record values) and QueryScientificRecordsFile (writes the full artifact to results_file but returns at most 100 preview rows inside a 20,000-character budget, omitting any single record that exceeds it). study_FLOW-0389.json is a single giant record (case_id='study') holding ~308 hull-level speed-grid observations (hull_id, 5 hull parameters, froude_number, residuary_resistance) nested inside data[0].observations, so its projected preview is dropped as oversized and the numbers never reach ExtractNumericColumns/CrossValidateRegressor/FitRidgeRegression. ExecuteNumericalCode cannot substitute: it has no filesystem or JSON access and only an allowlisted math/numpy surface, so the unseen 308 rows cannot be embedded or parsed. Without an inline complete-record reader (or a tool that consumes QueryScientificRecordsFile.results_file and yields typed numeric feature/target matrices), the declared repeated outer assessment cannot be applied to the actual hull-level speed-grid response, and selected_alpha_by_outer_seed for outer seeds 11/29/47, pooled_outer_assessment_rmse over the exact finite-assessment scope, and mean_selected_inner_cv_rmse (mean over outer assessments of the inner-CV criterion at each split's selected alpha) cannot be computed. A secondary gap is a nested/grouped CV-with-alpha-grid tool; that orchestration would otherwise be buildable from GroupTrainTestSplit (hull-level outer splits by seed) + CrossValidateRegressor (inner criterion, training-fold-only standardization) + FitRidgeRegression/PredictLinearModel (training-only standardization, held-out prediction) + RegressionMetrics (pooled held-out RMSE) + DescribeNumericData (mean of selected inner-CV RMSE).

ValueError: GraphRefinementLimit: diag_sd does not build diag(sd_i^2). It passes row_factors=[9,1,4] and column_factors=[9,1,4] to ScaleNumericMatrix using an identity matrix; ScaleNumericMatrix multiplies diagonal entry (i,i) by row_factor_i * column_factor_i, so the output diagonal becomes [81,1,16] instead of [9,1,4]. Consequently sigma would be [[81,0,0],[0,4,6],[0,6,16]] rather than the true covariance [[9,0,0],[0,4,6],[0,6,16]], corrupting the GLS weights/variance and the actual variance of the naive estimator.
